title: Release workflow fails closed on npm read-side lag: 1.36.0 published but 'not visible on npm' after ~5 minutes of polling
observation: Observed 2026-09-15 on the v1.36.0 release (run 34946709804). The publish step's `npm publish` succeeded (the version is on the registry with SLSA v1 provenance; `npm view @davesheffer/hunch dist-tags.latest` = 1.36.0 a few minutes later), but the same step then polled the registry for visibility from 08:33:57 to 08:39:03 and threw 'npm publication verification failed closed: @davesheffer/hunch@1.36.0 is not visible on npm'. The job is therefore red, and the following step 'Upload npm publication receipt' was skipped, so this release has no uploaded receipt artifact. This is the first release after the npm-publish environment approval was removed; the gate removal is unrelated to the lag. Consequence: a red run that is actually a successful publish; anyone reading the run (or an unattended retry) could conclude the release failed. Direction: lengthen the visibility poll with backoff (npm replication can lag well past five minutes), and make the receipt upload run when publish succeeded even if visibility verification timed out, marking visibility as 'unverified at T'. Do not retry publish blindly: the version already exists and a second publish would 403.
